summary: This Docker Compose configuration defines a development container service called 'app' that builds from a Dockerfile in the .devcontainer directory, passing in customizable build arguments for home directory, user ID, group ID, and username. It exposes a debug port, loads environment variables from files, mounts the project directory and VS Code extensions for persistence, and runs indefinitely to stay available for development work.

explanations.7: This passes the APP_HOME variable to the Docker build process, using the value of ${APP_HOME} from your environment, or defaulting to /app if it's not set.
explanations.8: Similarly, this passes the local user's numeric ID (UID) to Docker so the container user has matching permissions with your host machine; it defaults to 1000 if not provided.
explanations.9: This does the same thing for group ID (GID) so file ownership matches between your host and container.
explanations.10: This passes the username for the container user, defaulting to 'vscode' if not specified in your LOCAL_USER environment variable.
explanations.18: This mounts your current project directory (the dot) into the container at the APP_HOME path, so changes you make locally are immediately visible inside the container.
explanations.19: This creates a persistent named volume that stores VS Code extensions between container runs, so you don't have to reinstall them each time.
explanations.20: This mounts a bash history file from your .devcontainer folder into the container's home directory with read-write permissions, preserving your command history across container restarts.
explanations.22: The 'sleep infinity' command keeps the container running indefinitely instead of exiting, allowing you to attach and work inside it.
